chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

He was asked about a man who has two vessels containing water, and filth fell into one of them, but he does not know which of the two it is, and he is not able to obtain any water other than it. He said: “He pours them both out altogether and performs tayammum.”

key_terms.قَذَرٌ: filth or impurity contaminating the water
key_terms.لَا يَدْرِي: he does not know; indicating uncertainty
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute for wudu or ghusl
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُمَا: he pours them out or discards them

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if one of two water containers is najis but he does not know which one it is?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a case of uncertainty regarding najasah in two containers of water when no other water is available. The ruling is to discard both vessels and perform tayammum, showing precaution in ritual purity and the validity of tayammum when usable tahir water is not available.
